basis: 1A (Rose daily work plan, 2026-11-05): every release lane builds on its own runner, VM, storage, queue and lifecycle controller, so one lane's failure or cleanup cannot stop another; only genuinely shared atomic steps, such as app version allocation, may be serialized across lanes. This is the committed routing map, including explicitly retired legacy jobs for source auditing, and what each lane still needs. A host is listed only with values the committed route already uses or Infra's verified readback supplies, with its evidence; nothing here is a placeholder. A host builds only when it is in service and the lane is not retired: Mustang's shared-host route is permanently retired. Its dedicated lane file is identity-bound to the confirmed 2026-11-07 VM and data disk, but that runtime is unbound and the host is not in service. Yogi's counts once os/ota/yogi.json says builder.status ready. scripts/tests/test_lane_capacity.py derives routing from os-release.yml, release-pipeline.py and host configs and excludes retired lanes from capacity claims.
binding: Infra supplies verified readback (runner label carried only by that machine, VM project/zone/instance, storage root, lock path, queue, controller identity variable) and evidence. The named source owner then moves the lane and its dedicated workflow/controller routing together. Mustang owns its capacity-map change; Infra owns the common explicit-builder API. No proposed name is an actual host binding. Mustang's existing host field describes only retired legacy jobs, which may never run on Frankel again. The dedicated host entry is the confirmed VM and is not in service; runtime admission, runner registration and publication remain unbound. There is no fallback. Other target-own lanes retain their current route until explicitly changed.

frankel.note: Frankel keeps the existing builder once its storage is recovered. app-reuse and app-inputs-export read a Frankel attempt on this host, so they stay with Frankel.

mustang.note: The legacy host/workflow/modes above stay retired and cannot execute or use Frankel. The separate dedicated Mustang runtime is now source-bound for manual delivery with verified existing signer profile/scheduling and explicit budgets. Actual native/signer identity, capacity, source and output checks remain same-run requirements. No successful full run or extra parallel capacity is claimed.

agent.note: app-only builds on the Frankel builder: the public SDK, the pinned ZXing jar, the staged connection inputs and esbuild there, the app signer (PIXEL_APP_SIGNING_* through the signer identity), the 300 GiB free-space reserve and the builder-local app version ledger below, so it cannot leave that host. agent-hosted and agent-hosted-probe (1F, scripts/agent-hosted.py) run only on GitHub-hosted runners, with no controller, builder, storage or host lock: App's portable seam, the pinned public inputs, the signer identity admitted by its own probe, and the shared pixel-ota ledger (os/release-pipeline/agent/hosted.json reservation.store), which refuses until the Frankel builder records its consumed versions there (decision D2). They still share this workflow's one queue, so they claim no parallel capacity.

harness.note: 1E: the standalone compile harness has its own manual workflow, launcher3-compile.yml: its own queue, an owned controller and STOP from a per-run ownership record, and a worker routed only to the bound runner label. The os-release.yml launcher3-compile mode is removed. The host above names only where its earlier runs ran; Frankel's builder-reclaim launcher3-compile class still cleans their leftovers, and nothing routes there. The active binding is source-bound for the manual compile workflow only. This lane still claims no release or OTA capacity: runtimeStatus stays retired-shared-host, modes stay empty, and no os-release or OTA workflow reads the binding.

frankel-host-other.note: Not release lanes of the plan: retained-tree, alpha, signing, Models, Rango and Blazer work that reads this host's trees. They stay on it.

yogi.note: Its own workflow on main since #558: every self-hosted job runs on its runner, in its own queue, with its own controller and its own VM, disk and lock (os/ota/yogi.json). It builds once yogi.json builder.status is ready; until then scripts/yogi_ota.py refuses every stage. Any further Yogi stage stays inside this workflow, on this runner and queue.

appVersionLedger.store: scripts/release-allocate.py: pixel-ota releases (drafts included), this host's attempt directories and its rose-actions reservations, read and written under the host lock
appVersionLedger.note: latest-beta and app-only both allocate dev.pixel.voice versionCodes. Run on separate hosts with this store, they could choose the same version. So the ledger must first move to a store every lane can update atomically; that is the one cross-lane serialization the plan allows.
